label: early original-phase steps (t=1-4) reading n/f/s etc. after an h/u/v/i/x prefix
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase, at early positions t=1..4 (t=2 holds 64% of mass, t=3 25%); never at t=0, at the delimiter, or anywhere in the copy phase. The window (phase 0, 1<=t<=4) covers essentially all activations (recall 0.999) but only 3% of those steps fire, so token identity decides. It is strongest when the current input is n (26% of mass), f or s, and when the preceding tokens include h, u, v, i or x. The top activations are n right after h/u/v-type prefixes (e.g. v h u [n], h h [n], h u [n]). It favours first occurrences of the current token (in_first). The predicate (early step, input in {n,f,s,h,c,0,1}, prefix contains one of {h,u,v,i,x}) reaches dev F1 about 0.32 and mass recall 0.63. Many matching steps stay silent, which suggests a finer-grained lookup over (prefix, current token) combinations that no compact predicate captures.
